\section[el recibo]{el recibo — the receipt}

\label{lesson:ES-C491-recibo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the strike, then the Spanish for the business.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el recibo}
\textbf{el recibo} — \textquotedblleft{}the receipt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Guarde el recibo para cambiar el producto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Keep the receipt to exchange the item.}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\end{itemize}

\section[la propina]{la propina — the tip}

\label{lesson:ES-C491-propina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the cashier, then the Spanish for the wallet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la propina}
\textbf{la propina} — \textquotedblleft{}the tip\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le dejamos una propina al camarero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We left the waiter a tip.}
\end{quote}

In much of Latin America a waiter is \emph{el mesero}.
